lines: You set fire to my warehouse. With the rats still in it. I want you to think about the order of those two things.
Everything in that store belongs to everybody in this village. The rats were eating it. You were burning it. I do not see the improvement.
There is no warehouse. You are standing in what was the warehouse. The rats have gone to wherever rats go when the grain is ash, and I am a keeper of nothing.
I will stand here anyway. Somebody should.
lines_alt: Still nothing to keep. Still here. Do not ask me why; I have asked myself.

lines: That was the last of them. I know because I have kept this store eleven years and I know when a thing is over. Six waves. I counted every one.
You will want thanking. Consider it done. Now go and be somebody else's problem; the grain and I would like a quiet season.
I have been standing here listening to the pair of you throw Wards at each other in the road for {minutes_since_complaint} minutes while {pests_left} rats eat the winter.
If you want something to fight, it has six legs and it is in my grain. I am not asking twice.

lines.text: Gone, all of them, and every one of them cooked. I asked for rats gone, not for a kitchen. {food_burned} loads went up with them.
Gone, all of them, and every one of them cooked. I asked for rats gone, not for a kitchen. You kept the fire off the grain, I will give you that.

lines: The store is open. Mind the scorch marks; they are new.
Both of you, then. One on each side of the store, like you had planned it. I did not expect that, and I say so to your faces.

lines.text: And {burned_rats} of them burned. I will not ask which of you.

lines: The warehouse is open. Tell your mothers I said you did a day's work.
All of them, and all by you, while your friend did whatever your friend does. I noticed. The village notices more than you think.

lines.text: {burned_rats} of them by fire, which I did not enjoy, and the rest the proper way, which I did.

lines: The store is yours to walk through whenever you like. Mind the loose boards.
Rats are gone. Not by your hand, from what I saw, but gone. I thank whoever did it; I expect you know who.
That is the last of them. Good riddance. The store is open.

lines.text: Smoke in my grain store. You burned one. It worked, I grant you, and it took {food_burned} loads with it, which the rat would have taken a week over.
Smoke in my grain store. You burned one. It worked, I grant you, and nothing else caught, which is more luck than sense.

lines: {pests_left} to go. The big one does not burn so easily; I have seen people try.
There is nothing left. Not a ration, not a crust. {eaten_total} loads, and I counted every one of them go while the village's two wizards did whatever it is you do.
You may stop now. There is nothing left to defend. The rats will leave when they are hungry, which is more than I can say for anyone else.
lines_alt: Empty store. Rats in it anyway, out of habit. I know how they feel.

lines: {escapes} times I have watched a rat get the better of a wizard. I am not laughing. I want you to know that I am not laughing, because it is taking some effort.
Stand closer. Read the Ward. They only have the two colours; they are rats.
They are back. Wave {wave}, by my count. Fewer this time, and bolder. I told the elders we needed a cat; they said we needed a wizard. Well. Here you are.
lines_alt: They are back. They are always back. Rats are a kind of weather. Wave {wave}.
Wave {wave}. I have stopped being surprised and started being tired.

lines.text: {killed_total} down, {pests_left} to go. They eat faster than you fight; {eaten_total} loads gone since I first counted.
{killed_total} down, {pests_left} to go. Keep at it.
And one of them got away from you. They do that. Come at it again before it tells the others.
{burned_rats} of those by fire. I can smell it from here.

lines: Rats. In the Central Warehouse. {pests_total} of them at the last count, in and out of the grain like they pay rent.
Big ones. One of them is the size of a dog and clicks when it walks. Rats, I tell you. Nobody listens.
Store is quiet. Which is how I like it. Ask the carriers if you want news; I only count things.
lines_alt: Quiet. I do not trust it, but I will take it.
Nothing to report. Say that back to me slowly; I never hear it.

choices.text: What's the matter with the warehouse?
lines: I just told you. Rats. They go for the rations first, then the bread, then whatever smells of either. Every one you put down is a load saved.

They do not come out for the carriers and they do not come out for me. They will come out for you. Stand close to one and it will not run; they never run from a wizard. Then do whatever it is you do with the three colours.

choices.text: Those are not rats. They are machines. Look at the legs.
lines: They are rats. I have been keeper of this store for eleven years and I know a rat when it eats my grain.
Clicking is just what the big ones do.

choices.text: Six legs. Metal. It clicked at me.
lines: A rat with opinions, then. Put it down all the same.

choices.text: My teacher needs a log for the brazier. Could the store spare one?
lines: For {mentor}? Take one. Take it from the dry stack, not the green. And tell them the account is open; they never let it close.

choices.text: My teacher needs a log for the brazier. Could the store spare one?
lines: Not a log in the place. Ask the lumberjack, or wait for the carriers.
Mind the boards.
